name: Rotate By 90 Degrees
html:
Welcome back, dear reader. So, how is it going with the two-dimensional arrays? We hope you are following along and enjoying and understanding the concepts well. This interesting problem is called ROTATE BY 90 DEGREE.

Important Links: Problem link, Question video, Solution video

Problem Discussion:

We are given a square matrix and we have to rotate it by 90 degrees. (Refer to fig-1 for example). You may watch the question video to understand it and to get some hints.

Watch video

So, how did that go? Did you get any ideas from the question? Let's start our discussion and see how this problem can be solved.

Approach:
  1. Understanding The Pattern:
    So reader, have a look at fig-1. Do you observe something? The first row of the matrix has become the last column of the rotated matrix. Similarly, the second row of the matrix has become the 3rd (second-last) column of the matrix and so on. For now, let's forget about the numbers. Let's just concentrate on the fact that the rows of the matrix are becoming columns in the rotated matrix. Do you get something from this? (Think!). Well, we have a way of converting the rows of a matrix into columns and it is called the transpose of the matrix.
    • What is the Transpose of a matrix?
      The transpose of a matrix is nothing but just a flipped version of the matrix. When we exchange the rows and columns of a matrix such that each element A( i , j ) gets swapped with A( j , i ), then the matrix obtained is called the transpose of the given matrix. See(fig-2). So, we are going to transpose a matrix first so that we convert our rows to columns and vice-versa. If you have any doubts till here you may watch the solution video. Watch video
  2. Transposing The Matrix:
    So, we have now talked about transpose. We know what it is and we also know that we need to calculate it to rotate a matrix. The question is, how do we find the transpose? Since we know that transpose is a matrix in which M[i][j] gets interchanged with M[j][i], this is exactly what we are going to do.
    If we traverse the entire matrix and swap arr[i][j] with arr[j][i], it is not going to work and we will get the input matrix only as the result. Why is that so? Think!!!!!
    Well, this is happening because we are traversing the entire matrix. So, the values that were swapped earlier, got swapped again. Therefore we will not find any difference in the matrix. You may watch the solution video. So to overcome this problem we will perform swapping either only in the upper triangle of the matrix or only in the lower triangle of the matrix but not both. This is shown in the figure below:
    Watch video You may watch the solution video to understand this concept in depth. Watch video
  3. Reversing Each Row To Form Rotated Matrix:
    So, friend, you already know how to REVERSE AN ARRAY. If you want to revise it, you may refer to the REVERSE ANY ARRAY ARTICLE or you may refer to the REVERSE AN ARRAY SOLUTION VIDEO. We are just going to follow the same steps that we followed to reverse a 1-D array. We will have to reverse n rows now. Look at the diagram shown below:

The above figure shows that when we reverse each row of a transposed matrix we get our required rotated matrix. You should revisit the reversing procedure if you are facing any issues.

Algorithm:
  1. Input the matrix from the user.
  2. Transpose the matrix
  3. Reverse each row of the transposed matrix as you reverse a 1-D array.
import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); int[][] arr = new int[n][n]; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) { arr[i][j] = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); } } rotateby90(arr); display(arr); } public static void rotateby90(int[][] arr){ // transpose for(int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++){ for(int j = 0; j < i; j++){ int temp = arr[i][j]; arr[i][j]= arr[j][i]; arr[j][i] = temp; } } // reverse columns, row by row for(int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++){ int li = 0; int ri = arr[0].length - 1; while(li <= ri){ int temp = arr[i][li]; arr[i][li] = arr[i][ri]; arr[i][ri] = temp; li++; ri--; } } } public static void display(int[][] arr){ for(int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++){ for(int j = 0; j < arr[0].length; j++){ System.out.print(arr[i][j] + " "); } System.out.println(); } } }
java; true"; Analysis Time Complexity:

The time complexity for rotating the matrix by this procedure is O(n2) as for transposing we are traversing the upper triangle i.e. we are traversing n2/2 elements and then reversing takes O(n) time and we have to reverse n rows. So it becomes O(n2 + n2/2) which is O(n2).

SPACE COMPLEXITY:

The space complexity is O(1) as we are transposing and then reversing in-place and we are not consuming any auxiliary memory.

Dear reader, we hope that you have now understood the entire procedure of rotating a matrix by 900 . If you still have any doubts you can watch the complete solution video to clear them.

Watch video Suggestions:

Here are some suggestions from us that you don't want to miss:

  1. This problem was basic but required the use of transpose of a matrix, which is a mathematical topic. There are various mathematical topics that you will require as we move forward. But don't worry, you just require some basic knowledge.
  2. If you want to pursue competitive programming you have to be good at mathematics. Start working on those aspects as well.
  3. In interviews, you will see matrix-based problems a lot which come under difficult topics like dynamic programming. So, we will be exploring matrices in-depth and a lot in later sections. So, be with us on this journey together. Happy Coding!
